scenarios.description: A Codex role with a wildcard allowlist: the child's generated config declares only production Neotoma; none of the operator's personal servers, and the isolated home is removed afterwards.
The same for Cursor, which is also given an explicit --workspace (the directory its project configuration is checked for).
A role granted two Neotoma tools: the Codex child's only server exposes exactly those.
A role whose allowlist grants no Neotoma tools needs no token and launches with no MCP server at all.
A role granted Neotoma tools without a token of its own: no child starts, and the envelope names the setting to repair (never a value). The operator's bearer is never substituted.
NEOTOMA_BASE_URL is not an https endpoint: no child starts and the envelope names it.

The workspace's project root carries its own Cursor MCP file, which Cursor would load for --workspace (here declaring a server under the allowed name). No child starts; the envelope names the file to repair.
A dispatch forced to Fly (not configured here) is refused, and never builds a local isolated home or starts a local child.
